'''Matarbari LNG power station''' is a cancelled power station in Maheshkhali Upazila - Cox's Bazar District, Chittagong, Bangladesh.

==Background==

Japanese MITSUI and Company Limited and the Coal Power Generation Company Bangladesh Limited (CPGCBL) will jointly build a regasified liquefied natural gas power plant.<ref>Aminur Rahman Rasel [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/power-energy/2017/07/18/govt-plans-build-600mw-power-plant-matarbari Govt plans to build 600MW LNG-based power plant at Matarbari], ''Dhaka Tribune'', Jul 18, 2017</ref>

'''In April 2019''', CPGCBL put out a request for financial advisory services for the project.<ref>[https://cpgcbl.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/cpgcbl.portal.gov.bd/page/9c33abb5_e666_4a96_95b9_1e1a80f6720b/Final-FAS-EOI-Notice-r4.pdf REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EoI) FOR SELECTION OF CONSULTANT FOR FINANCIAL ADVISORY SERVICES (FAS).], CPGCBL website, Apr 4, 2019</ref>

By the end of '''2019''', CPGCBL had purchased the land for the power plant.<ref name=name/>

One of the deals involves the local Summit Group, Japan's Mitsubishi Corporation and the US's General Electric Company, Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) and GE Switzerland. At an event in Bidyut Bhaban, BPDB and GE Switzerland decided to form a joint venture company to implement the project. The joint venture will conduct a feasibility study, develop 5,600 acres of land, construct and operate the power plant, and construct an LNG import terminal and infrastructure.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/74b-deals-inked-produce-6000mw-1603933|title=$7.4b deals inked to produce 6,000MW|date=2018-07-12|work=The Daily Star|access-date=2022-08-17|language=en}}</ref> 

The estimated project cost includes US $1.6 billion for land development and US $2.8 billion for the power plant. The expected completion time is 36 months.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/74b-deals-inked-produce-6000mw-1603933|title=$7.4b deals inked to produce 6,000MW|date=2018-07-12|work=The Daily Star|access-date=2022-08-17|language=en}}</ref>
